newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler to sell Pentastar Electronics unit.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to sell Pentastar Electronics unit.

text.p: Chrysler Corp., moving to divest its last defence subsidary, said Monday it agreed to sell Pentastar Electronics Inc. to a management-led investment group for an undisclosed price.
Pentastar Electronics, based in Huntsville, Ala., produces automatic test equipment for military applications. It has about 350 employees and had 1995 sales of about $50 million.
Terms of the sale to PEI Acquisition Corp. were not announced. Closing of the transaction is expected to occur within 60 days and is subject to customary conditions, Chrysler said.
The investment group includes the managers at Pentastar Electronics, plus additional outside investors, whom a Chrysler spokeswoman declined to identify.

Details on the defence electronics firm's future operational structure were not immediately available, but the spokeswoman said the company will no longer use the Pentastar name because of conflicts with Chrysler's trademark.
The transaction will complete Chrysler's plans to divest all of its aerospace and defence businesses.
The automaker in June sold Electrospace Systems Inc., a defence electronics unit, and Chrysler Technologies Airborne Systems Inc. to Raytheon Co.'s E-Systems Inc. unit for $475 million.
Chrysler has also said it wants to divest other non-core businesses, such as its Dollar and Thrifty rental car chains, in accordance with its commitment to focus on its core automotive business.
Chrysler's stock rose 37.5 cents to $34.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
